01 / Telecom & Secure Communications

Modernizing telecom.
Working with legacy constraints.

A secure communications platform with an aging database, hardware-bound licenses, and no room for an extended outage. Led the database migration and designed its automated recovery path.

Aurora PostgreSQL · AWS DMS · Lambda · Terraform

Automated

Failover recovery in one automated workflow

Recovery, service validation and licensed service identity handled together
Architectural contribution
  • Led the database modernization: a phased migration with a controlled cutover to Aurora PostgreSQL, planned around a legacy platform with no room for extended downtime.
  • Designed the failover architecture: replaced a manual, hardware-dependent recovery process with an automated, serverless failover path.
  • Preserved licensing continuity: designed a networking approach that kept hardware-bound software licenses valid through the cloud transition.
  • Implemented data protection: migrated the existing key-management integration to AWS KMS while preserving application compatibility.

02 / Tolling Infrastructure

Tolling platforms.
One cloud foundation.

Several tolling projects each had their own AWS setup for toll collection and roadside systems. I designed one shared landing zone with consistent networking, security guardrails, and automated provisioning, plus a JSM webhook integration and private S3 image APIs.

AWS Organizations · Transit Gateway · API Gateway · S3 · Route 53 · Terraform

Weeks → hours

New environment provisioning

40+ AWS accounts under one governance model
Architectural contribution
  • Designed the landing zone: a modular, tiered Terraform structure separating foundation, networking, shared services, and applications.
  • Centralized the network design: a hub-and-spoke model that replaced fragmented, per-account networking with one consistent pattern.
  • Reduced provisioning time: automated environment setup that previously took weeks of manual configuration.
  • Simplified security oversight: centralized logging and monitoring across all accounts for a single, consistent audit trail.
  • Centralized DNS across accounts: shared public and private Route 53 zones with Resolver forwarding, using an explicit authorization-then-association workflow for consumer VPCs.

03 / Healthcare & Cost Architecture

A clinical platform,
built to grow beyond its hardware.

Decomposed a legacy clinical monolith into managed, containerized services and reduced database pressure with caching. Related cost optimization and FinOps architecture extended across several client engagements.

Amazon EKS · RDS · ElastiCache · CloudFront

~50%

Less direct database read load

$300K+ annual savings identified across engagements
Architectural contribution
  • Re-architected a legacy monolith: decomposed an on-premise clinical application into containerized services running on managed infrastructure, removing the on-prem hardware dependency.

  • Applied cost-aware compute design: moved static server fleets to dynamic, right-sized compute across several engagements.
  • Standardized delivery pipelines: automated deployment and disaster-recovery processes to reduce manual operational overhead.

04 / AWS APN & Migration Engagements

Cloud migration acceleration.
From discovery to business case.

Enterprise cloud discovery, migration readiness assessments (MRA), and directional business cases across AWS Partner Network (APN) consulting engagements. Led infrastructure profiling, TCO modeling, and target architecture blueprints.

AWS Transform · Application Discovery Service · VMware vCenter · RVTools · AWS CAF

$2.5M+

Projected 3-year TCO savings

1,000+ servers profiled across EU & US facilities
Architectural contribution
  • Automated enterprise inventory discovery: deployed agentless collectors in VMware vCenter and loaded RVTools exports to capture real CPU, RAM, disk, and network-dependency data without installing agents on every server.
  • Led Kubernetes & VMware modernization: evaluated on-premises VMware Tanzu and Dell VxRail estates, and designed target Amazon EKS platforms with Karpenter autoscaling and Graviton compute to remove hypervisor licensing costs.
  • Generated executive Directional Business Cases: used AWS Transform to model 3–5 year TCO comparisons, right-sized EC2 compute, and optimized licensing (BYOL vs. License Included) to qualify for AWS MAP funding.
  • Assessed Migration Readiness (MRA): evaluated organizations across all 6 AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (CAF) pillars to identify operational, security, and governance gaps prior to migration mobilization.
  • Designed target cloud environments: mapped legacy monolithic services to managed AWS services (EKS, Aurora, IoT Core) and designed cloud marketplace onboarding.

05 / Enterprise Hybrid Cloud Infrastructure

21 nodes, no shared SAN,
zero downtime at peak load.

Designed a 21+ node active-active Oracle RAC cluster on AWS using software-defined clustered storage to work around AWS's lack of native shared-SAN block storage, plus a hybrid object storage platform and automated disaster recovery spanning AWS, on-prem VMware, and OpenStack.

Oracle RAC · FlashGrid · AWS EC2/EBS · MinIO · Zimbra

21+

Active Oracle RAC nodes on AWS, without native shared-SAN storage

Mail failover cut from 4+ hours of manual recovery to under 3 minutes
Architectural contribution
  • Built a 21+ node Oracle RAC cluster on AWS: used software-defined clustered storage to emulate shared-SAN semantics across independently-attached EBS volumes, tuning ASM diskgroups and kernel I/O settings for sub-2ms latency under peak concurrency.
  • Automated end-to-end disaster recovery for enterprise mail: built a single script handling elastic IP reassociation, EBS volume reattachment, and service recovery, cutting RTO from 4+ hours to under 3 minutes.
  • Unified storage across three infrastructure environments: deployed a distributed S3-compatible object storage platform reachable from AWS, an on-prem VMware data center, and OpenStack behind one API.
  • Cut recurring storage costs by 40%: automated lifecycle tiering from hot object storage to AWS S3 Glacier while meeting multi-year audit retention requirements.

06 / Independent Products & AI-Assisted Engineering

NexusCore AI: one system for joiners, movers & leavers.
Reliable workflows, cited policy answers, sub-5s offboarding.

A platform that brings account access, joiner-mover-leaver (JML) automation, attendance, and HR policy answers into one place, instead of a dozen disconnected tools. It runs on Temporal workflows, keeps a tamper-evident (SHA-256) audit trail, and keeps each customer's data separate. It targets the modelled ~$1,400 per employee that scattered identity tooling costs.

FastAPI · Next.js 15 · Temporal SDK · PostgreSQL 16 · Amazon EKS · ArgoCD · Terraform

$240K/yr

Modelled net TCO savings (66.7% for a 500-employee company)

Sub-5s de-provisioning · 509 passing tests · 89% modelled ticket deflection
Architectural contribution
  • Built joiner, mover, and leaver workflows on Temporal: multi-step account changes across SaaS tools that retry with backoff and undo earlier steps if a later one fails, so no half-removed accounts are left behind.
  • Built policy answers that cite their source: keyword (BM25) plus vector search that quotes the exact clause heading and handbook page, with each customer's documents kept strictly separate.
  • Added per-team access profiles: ready-made access bundles for teams such as SecOps, DevOps, and Tier-2 Support, with a checklist HR works through before anything is provisioned.
  • Set up GitOps delivery on AWS: six services in separate repos, deployed with Helm to Amazon EKS and kept in sync by ArgoCD, with secrets from External Secrets Operator (and a simpler single-EC2 Docker option).
  • Put AI-assisted development on a short leash: written working rules, 509 automated tests across 5 suites (all passing), and guardrails that block raw HTML controls.

02 / How I work

I work across the parts that usually get split between teams.

I design the platform and I help build it. That usually means setting up the foundation, moving workloads onto it, keeping costs in check, and making sure it stays healthy after launch.

[01]

Cloud foundations
& DevOps

Turning scattered AWS accounts into one well-run platform, with Terraform, CI/CD, a clear account structure, networking, and guardrails that make the safe option the easy one.

[02]

Migration &
modernization

Moving old databases and monolithic apps in careful stages, so the business keeps running while the new setup gains better recovery options and gets easier to operate.

[03]

Security, identity
& automation

Setting clear authentication and authorization boundaries, automating releases, and layering controls so security doesn't hinge on one app or on someone remembering a manual step.

[04]

FinOps &
SRE thinking

Tying cost back to design decisions: right-sizing, caching, monitoring, and automatic recovery, so systems stay up and people spend less time fighting fires.
